title: 2 high school grads injured, lane closed after shooting on the Dan Ryan - NewsBreak
text: CHICAGO ( WGN ) — A pair of high school graduates were injured and traffic lanes were condensed after a shooting on the Dan Ryan Expressway Wednesday afternoon. According to the Illinois State Police, troopers were called to I-90 northbound near West 43rd Street around 2 p.m. for a report of shots fired. ISP said injuries have been reported—later confirming two people were shot and taken to the hospital—and one lane of traffic on the northbound Dan Ryan is currently closed. A mother told WGN-TV her two sons and some of their friends were on their way to Six Flags when there was a road rage incident and someone in another car started shooting at them. She said those in the car with her sons were all recent high school graduates with plans to go off to college in the fall. It is unclear what condition the two people who were shot are in, but WGN-TV did speak with a witness who heard about the shooting, and saw the two victims being loaded into an ambulance. “One was laying down, one was sitting up on the stretcher,” Montrel Grady said. “They was trying to hurry up and put him up on a stretcher and hurry up and put them on the ambulance.” Police have no one in custody. The investigation is active and ongoing with no further information at this time. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to WGN-TV.
